diagram_math_checks.data: For i=1,...,N, theta_i belongs to K; ell:S x K -> [0,1]; d_pi_i and d_hatpi_i are normalized state probability vectors. L_i(theta_i) and S_i are real bounded expectations under different occupancies.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Local def-imitation-learning-and-expert-surrogate-loss Definition and theorem [F1], [F2], [A1]. Diagram arrows are deductions, explicitly not policy-space maps.

diagram_math_checks.relation: N^{-1} sum_i L_i(theta_i) <= epsilon_N + R_N/N and sum_i min(1,T beta_i) <= M_N.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The top boxes reproduce theorem steps 1.1 and 1.2 exactly with R_N=1+(4G^2/mu)H_{N-1} and M_N=k_alpha(q_T+2); these abbreviations retain the harmonic and geometric-mixing errors.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Both top boxes feed N^{-1} sum_i S_i <= B_N.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Theorem [F4] and local lem-dagger-mixture-occupancy apply to g(s)=ell(s,theta_i) in [0,1], giving S_i <= L_i(theta_i)+min(1,T beta_i). Average, then insert both top bounds (steps 2.1 and 3.1) to obtain B_N=epsilon_N+(R_N+M_N)/N.

diagram_math_checks.relation: There exists i in {1,...,N} with S_i <= B_N, with hatpi=hatpi_i.
diagram_math_checks.justification: N is positive and finite. Some S_i is at most their arithmetic average; otherwise summing strict inequalities contradicts the average. This is exactly step 3.1, and makes no claim that the last iterate is selected.
Theorem [A4], [F5] and local lem-dagger-task-cost-from-expert-surrogate give J(hatpi_i)-J(pi*) <= uT S_i. Since u>=0 and T>=1, substituting S_i<=B_N preserves direction (step 4.1), including u=0.
